jobs.title: Sr. Interdisciplinary Systems Engineer / Architect, AWS Bespoke Solutions
jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

The Bespoke Solutions group in AWS Region Services is looking for a Interdisciplinary Systems Engineer with technical leadership experience leading hardware, software, and FGPA developers through the systems engineering lifecycle from conception to delivery.
  
  
We develop AWS owned hardware solutions in order to scale globally, minimize cost, and maximize value for our customers. We are a growing team of hardware, software and FPGA engineers with a dedicated product development lab in Arlington, VA.  
  
You will perform system/product definition, requirements decomposition, technical risk assessments, and end to end testing for scalable high assurance embedded systems in the AWS technology ecosystem.  
  
As a member of the Bespoke Solutions Team in Region Services, you will be joining a talented full-stack development team (hardware and software) that is laser-focused on developing network security products that enable our Amazon Dedicated Cloud to operate efficiently at scale.  
  
This position requires that the candidate selected must currently possess and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance. The position further requires that, after start, the selected candidate obtain and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance with polygraph or commensurate clearance for each government agency for which they perform AWS work.  
  
Key job responsibilities  

* Evaluate, develop, and deliver solutions for the lifecycle of complex interdisciplinary system design problems for which the technical strategy is frequently not defined
* Derive requirements for system efficiency, operational excellence, and user experience.
* Lead design and system engineers to perform verification and validation of certification requirements.
* Generate technical artifacts that ensure design completeness and improve system traceability.
* Lead design meetings to plan development and review peer designs.
* Test/verify new technologies to improve the customer experience.
* Mentor and educate other engineers on systems goals and constraints in relation to physical, interfaces, compliance, data management, and risk management.

  
A day in the life  
You will be a technical leader on a cross-functional team of hardware and software developers, focusing on system-level integration and verification. You will help set and maintain the standard for system testing and verification, understanding and planning for the impact of team decisions on overall system architecture in team meetings, design reviews, and through written documents. You will lead architectural discussions, and strategic planning meetings.  
  
You will use and develop CI/CD pipelines to automatically run your own unit tests, and hardware in the loop tests. You help deploy embedded software onto hardware targets and help debug issues that come along in RTL, hardware, or software. You will develop and document software sub-systems and components in Rust, you will coordinate with the team daily to make design decisions, resolve blockers, and review code.  
  
You will guide system architecture development and trade studies for encryption devices, key management systems, FPGAs, and ASICs. You will generate artifacts for design reviews (SRR, PDR, CDR, TRR) as part of the government certification processes. You will work with various teams to establish requirements, develop verification methods, and ensure system specifications are met. You will use tools such as Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) or Systems Modeling Language (SysML) to create and maintain system documentation, including test procedures, requirements documentation, and verification matrices.
  
  
You will demonstrate a high standard, help prioritize development activities and educate others about systems engineering best practices and tools.  
  
About the team  
About AWS
  
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.  
  
Why AWS?  
Our team is dedicated to supporting new members. We have a broad mix of experience levels and tenures, and we’re building an environment that celebrates knowledge-sharing and mentorship. Our senior members enjoy one-on-one mentoring and thorough, but kind, code reviews. We care about your career growth and strive to assign projects that help our team members develop your engineering expertise so you feel empowered to take on more complex tasks in the future.  
  
AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS)  
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.
  
  
Diverse Experiences  
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.
  
  
Inclusive Team Culture  
AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

jobs.title: Controls Engineer 2
jobs.description:
Company Overview: Hamilton Medical was founded in 1983 with a clear mission: to enhance the lives of patients on respirators and support the caregivers who serve them. Our focus is on developing ventilation technologies that prioritize safety, effectiveness, and lung protection. We are dedicated to easing the burden on healthcare professionals who work tirelessly every day, helping critically ill patients recover and regain their health. We are committed to helping medical teams deliver the best respiratory care ‑ to anyone, anywhere. Responsibilities:

Hamilton Medical, Inc. (HMI) is seeking a Controls Engineer 2 who will take technical ownership of the control systems for all automated equipment at HMI. This role maintains and improves PLC, HMI, and robot programs to increase equipment reliability, process yield, and production efficiency. The Controls Engineer 2 works with Manufacturing Engineering to optimize automation, supports Maintenance in troubleshooting equipment errors, and coordinates technical activities with external automation vendors. The role independently executes assigned controls work with occasional guidance on complex issues. A strong candidate solves problems efficiently, creates practical solutions, documents changes, shares knowledge, and supports safe, consistent production.

**Essential Job Functions:**

* Takes technical ownership of control systems for all automated equipment at HMI, maintaining reliable operation and serving as the primary internal controls resource.
* Develops, modifies, tests, and maintains PLC and HMI programs, including machine sequences, alarms, diagnostics, recipes, and process settings.
* Programs, debugs, and optimizes robots, including motion paths, tooling interfaces, equipment handshakes, and fault recovery sequences.
* Integrates and troubleshoots sensors, actuators, servo drives, machine vision, and other peripheral devices through PLC interfaces and industrial communication networks.
* Partners with manufacturing engineers to analyze cycle time, downtime, faults, and yield, and implements controls improvements that increase automation performance and process consistency to attain target OEE KPIs.
* Supports Maintenance in troubleshooting control system errors and restoring equipment operation, and investigates recurring failures and implements corrective actions with Engineering and Quality.
* Coordinates external automation vendors for troubleshooting, modifications, and upgrades, reviews technical deliverables and obtains current source programs, backups, and documentation for HMI support.
* Translates manufacturing needs into controls requirements and functional specifications, reviews proposed hardware, software, and vendor designs for maintainability and compatibility with HMI equipment.
* Coordinates controls startup, debugging, and commissioning for new and modified equipment, supports factory acceptance testing, site acceptance testing, and production handoff.
* Applies and improves programming standards, reusable code, and documentation practices, maintains controlled program versions, verified backups, change histories, and recovery instructions.
* Develops and executes controls test plans, including affected functions and fault recovery, supports equipment qualification and validation with Manufacturing Engineering and Quality.
* Assesses controls changes for effects on machine safety, product quality, and validated processes, follows HMI change control, testing, and release requirements.
* Maintains electrical schematics, I/O lists, network layouts, program comments, and troubleshooting guides, supports equipment data collection for diagnostics and performance analysis.
* Trains Maintenance, Manufacturing Engineering, and production personnel on controls, diagnostics, and recovery procedures appropriate to their roles.
* Plans assigned controls projects and upgrades, including obsolete component replacement, estimates resources, communicates schedules and risks, and coordinates downtime with Production and Maintenance.
* Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

* Independently uses first-principles thinking and structured troubleshooting, seeks assistance when technical complexity or risk requires additional expertise.
* Shows initiative, takes ownership of assigned tasks, and completes work without repeated prompting.
* Proficient in PLC programming and troubleshooting, HMI development, and robot programming for automated manufacturing equipment.
* Working knowledge of sensors, actuators, servo systems, variable frequency drives, machine vision interfaces, and industrial communication networks.
* Ability to read electrical schematics and use diagnostic tools to distinguish programming, electrical, mechanical, and process-related faults.
* Ability to evaluate equipment performance data and apply root cause analysis techniques to recurring faults and production losses.
* Working knowledge of machine safety functions, interlocks, and safe troubleshooting practices, follows established equipment safety procedures.
* Excellent communication and documentation skills, works effectively with manufacturing engineers, maintenance technicians, production personnel, Quality, and external vendors.
* Ability to prioritize competing production needs, communicate realistic completion dates, and support planned installations and production recovery activities.

Education/Experience:

* 3+ years of technical experience in controls engineering or industrial automation, including hands-on PLC programming and troubleshooting.
* Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, Automation Engineering, Mechatronics, or a closely related engineering discipline required.
* Experience programming and supporting industrial robots in manufacturing applications required.
* Experience with PLC and HMI platforms such as Allen-Bradley, Siemens, Beckhoff, or comparable systems, ability to learn and support multiple platforms.

Summary
  
  
We are seeking a highly skilled and experienced machine learning engineer to join AIML Evaluation to build the systems that evaluate and refine Apple's foundation models and agents. As a key member of the team, you will help design and develop benchmarks, evaluators, simulation environments, and prompt and context optimization pipelines that drive quality improvements across Apple's AI experiences. You will collaborate with product teams and the foundation model team to close the loop between observation and improvement, contributing datasets, environments, and reward signals that drive model and agent quality.
  
  
Description
  
  
Most model evaluation stops at a scorecard. The failing traces get thrown away, even though they're the most relevant training signal we have. Our team puts them to work. We evaluate across offline benchmarks, device-in-the-loop simulation, and on-device observation in production, and we turn what we find into persona-grounded datasets and reward signals for foundation model post-training. In this role, you will build the systems that connect failure analysis to measurable model and agent improvements across a broad range of AI products at Apple. The path from finding a problem to fixing it is short: the loop you build finds the failure, produces the data and checks the result. The work reaches millions of users.
  
  
Minimum Qualifications  
  
  

* Strong background in machine learning and distributed systems.
* A proven track record of solving ambiguous problems end to end: defining the problem and the metric, building the solution, and showing measured impact.
* Experience leading technical work across multiple codebases, teams, and organizations.
* Experience building and maintaining ML infrastructure for evaluation, training, or deployment.
* 6+ years of professional experience as a software engineer, preferably in machine learning or a related field. Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  
  
  
Preferred Qualifications  
  
  

* Experience with LLM evaluation, LLM-as-judge, or reward modeling.
* Experience with prompt optimization, agent harness development, or post-training (SFT, DPO, RLHF).
* Proficiency in Python and ML frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX.
* Experience with agentic systems, simulation environments, or trajectory-based data generation.
* Familiarity with on-device or privacy-preserving ML.
* Understanding of how training data is used in post-training and how data choices affect model behavior.
* Excellent communication skills.

  
  
  
At Apple, base pay is one part of our total compensation package and is determined within a range. This provides the opportunity to progress as you grow and develop within a role. The base pay range for this role is between $175,000 and $308,500, and your base pay will depend on your skills, qualifications, experience, and location.  
  
Apple employees also have the opportunity to become an Apple shareholder through participation in Apple’s discretionary employee stock programs. Apple employees are eligible for discretionary restricted stock unit awards, and can purchase Apple stock at a discount if voluntarily participating in Apple’s Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You’ll also receive benefits including: Comprehensive medical and dental coverage, retirement benefits, a range of discounted products and free services, and for formal education related to advancing your career at Apple, reimbursement for certain educational expenses — including tuition. Additionally, this role might be eligible for discretionary bonuses or commission payments as well as relocation. Learn more about Apple Benefits  
  
Note: Apple benefit, compensation and employee stock programs are subject to eligibility requirements and other terms of the applicable plan or program.  
  
  

Apple is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to inclusion and diversity. We seek to promote equal opportunity for all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, Veteran status, or other legally protected characteristics. jobs.title: Principal Electrical Engineer – Power Electronics & CT Architecture
jobs.description:
**Job Description Summary**
===========================

Join GE HealthCare's CT Engineering team and help define how electrical power is designed, distributed and managed across our next generation of CT systems.  
  
We're looking for an experienced Power Electronics Engineer who enjoys solving complex system-level problems and wants to stay actively involved in the engineering work. This is a hands-on technical leadership role, not an oversight position. You'll help set the architecture and technical direction while also designing, analyzing, troubleshooting, testing, and solving problems alongside the team.  
  
In this role, you'll work across multiple circuit boards and electrical subsystems to help define the overall power architecture of our CT platforms. You'll influence long-term technical strategy while continuing to design, analyze, prototype, troubleshoot and test real hardware.  
  
This is an exciting opportunity for someone who has built deep expertise in power electronics and is ready to expand their influence from individual circuit and board design into broader system architecture and technical leadership.  
  
Location: Waukesha, Wisconsin, hybrid with approximately 3 days onsite  
  
Relocation assistance: Available

**Job Description**
===================

### **What You'll Do**

* Define and evolve electrical power architecture for advanced CT systems.
* Design analog and power electronics circuitry, including power conversion, controls and high-speed interfaces.
* Develop electrical architectures spanning multiple boards, components and subsystems.
* Create and review schematics and PCB designs using ECAD tools.
* Lead technical design reviews and promote strong engineering rigor and best practices.
* Build and evaluate prototypes and conduct hands-on troubleshooting, validation and reliability testing.
* Take designs from concept through prototype, verification and production support.
* Partner with digital, systems, mechanical, manufacturing, service and global engineering teams to solve complex design challenges.
* Balance performance, reliability, manufacturability, cost and regulatory requirements when making design decisions.
* Help shape longer-term power electronics strategy for future CT platforms.

### **What You'll Bring**

* Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering.
* 7+ years of professional electrical engineering experience.
* Strong hands-on experience with **power electronics and power conversion**.
* Experience designing and analyzing electrical circuits, including schematic design and simulation.
* Experience with PCB design/layout and schematic capture.
* Experience taking electrical designs from concept through prototype, testing and production support.
* Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to communicate technical concepts clearly across engineering teams.

### **We'd Love to See**

Experience in one or more of the following is helpful, but **you don't need to check every box**:

* Switching power supplies, converters or power distribution systems.
* Buck/boost or resonant converter design.
* High-power or higher-voltage electrical systems.
* EMC-conscious design and troubleshooting.
* Design for reliability and manufacturability.
* UL, ETL, IEC or other applicable regulatory standards.
* Digital electronics or FPGA/VHDL.
* Leading complex technical designs or influencing system-level architecture.

### **Why This Role?**

**This is a working architect role, not an oversight role.** You'll help set the power architecture strategy for our CT platforms while remaining actively involved in the engineering. You'll work directly with schematics, circuits, PCBs, prototypes, testing, troubleshooting, and design reviews while also providing technical direction across the broader system.

It's a great opportunity for an experienced power electronics engineer who wants to **stay close to the technology while growing their influence from board-level design into system-level architecture and technical leadership.**

This isn't an architecture role where you'll step away from engineering.

You'll have the opportunity to **stay hands-on while expanding your technical influence**, helping determine how power moves through an incredibly complex medical imaging system.

You'll work with a large multidisciplinary engineering organization, collaborate globally, solve difficult technical problems and help set the direction for future CT platforms.

For an experienced power electronics engineer who's ready to grow from **board-level design into system-level technical leadership**, this role offers a very natural next step.

jobs.title: Senior Security Firmware Engineer, Data Center Systems
jobs.description:
NVIDIA's invention of the GPU in 1999 sparked the growth of the PC gaming market, redefined modern computer graphics, and revolutionized parallel computing. GPU deep learning ignited the modern AI era, with NVIDIA hardware and software acting as the foundation for the world's most ambitious AI, robotics, and autonomous systems workloads. Today, we are the AI computing company. NVIDIA Data Center Systems, including DGX, HGX, and MGX platforms, deliver the world's leading infrastructure for AI at scale. We are growing our teams with the most thoughtful, creative, and driven people on the planet.

NVIDIA is searching for a highly motivated and creative senior security firmware engineer to join the Data Center Systems Software team and secure the platform: the baseboard management controllers, microcontrollers, and silicon roots of trust the rest of the platform depends on. You will design and deliver the firmware that proves the integrity of NVIDIA's data center systems from the first instruction out of reset through attestation, update, and recovery in production, and set technical direction for work that spans silicon vendors, platform teams, and industry standards bodies.

What You'll Be Doing

Derive security requirements for NVIDIA’s data center platforms from business needs and threat modeling.
Design and deliver root of trust firmware with features like secure and measured boot, attestation, provisioning of identities and cryptographic material, and secure debug.
Own features from architecture to code: make the trade-offs explicit, gain agreement across silicon, platform, security architecture, manufacturing, and partner teams, and deliver the implementation.
Implement industry security standards (eg.: SPDM, TCG DICE).
Lead design and code reviews, improve threat modeling, testing, CI, and release practices, and make AI agents a normal part of how the team builds firmware.

What We Need To See

BS or MS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
7+ years of software and firmware engineering experience, or equivalent depth, including products built on a hardware root of trust.
Deep understanding of roof of trust security fundamentals: chains of trust, signing and key management, attestation, and anti-rollback.
Strong low-level programming skills and a deep understanding of SoC access controls (privilege levels, TrustZone, memory and bus protection).
Familiarity with server firmware and systems software, plus experience building automation using Python or a comparable language.
A record of leading technical work across teams without formal authority, including guiding other engineers on a shared deliverable.
Experience with modern AI and agents, including an AI-forward mindset and proactive adoption of new tools and techniques.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a strong preference for written communication that creates clarity and institutional memory for a distributed team.
Comfortable with ambiguity and complexity; you make sound decisions quickly with incomplete information and course-correct without friction.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Contributions to open-source root of trust projects or to industry security standards.
Experience building systems with symmetric, asymmetric, and post-quantum cryptography.
Rust firmware experience, including bringing Rust into an existing C or C++ codebase.
Secure Manufacturing at scale. Security certifications such as FIPS 140-3.
Hardware cryptographic accelerators, secure key storage, trusted execution frameworks such as OP-TEE or Keystone, and OpenBMC.

jobs.title: R&D Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Job Description:

The Elevator Pitch: Why will you enjoy this new opportunity?

The Virtual Machine Monitor Group (“Monitor Group”) is responsible for the core CPU and memory virtualization technology used in all of Broadcom's VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) Division products. You will have the opportunity to work with bleeding edge CPU technology, VT-x/AMD-V, interrupt virtualization, memory virtualization/management, and virtualization of other forms of compute technologies and accelerators.

The VCF Division works to build products and solutions that power the hybrid cloud. Working alongside other highly motivated and capable engineers you will get to interact with our largest customers to define the next generation of Broadcom's industry-leading VMWare Cloud Foundation platform.

Success in the Role: What are the performance outcomes over the first 6-12 months you will work toward completing?

The Monitor Group’s principal function is to maintain and develop the virtual CPU and memory aspects of the virtual machine platform that runs guest operating systems.

In the first 6 months, you will be expected to get up to speed with one of the specialization areas, such as new CPU feature enablement, x86_64 instruction set (ISA) virtualization, confidential computing, modernization of the monitor architecture, hardware accelerators, power-aware compute or aspects of guest timekeeping. By year 1 you would be expected to have impactful, core engineering contributions and enhancements in your area of specialization.

The Work: What type of work will you be doing? What assignments, requirements, or skills will you be performing on a regular basis?

This role requires you to possess a deep understanding of processor architecture and low-level OS kernel internals, system software including memory management, resource management, and interrupt architecture. The principal programming language used is C, with assembly code used whenever needed to deal with machine-specific constructs.

You will work independently and as a member of a team of software engineers to design and deliver features in support of new processors or a proposed enhancement for the virtual machine monitor architecture. As an example, you might be involved in the design and implementation of upcoming CPU instruction set updates in a virtualization context. Similarly, you may be assigned to contribute to an aspect of memory virtualization/management features as part of a monitor modernization effort. For more senior roles you would be expected to make proposals that help define the design roadmap, or drive a technical effort leading other engineers.

What is the leadership like for this role? What is the structure and culture of the team like?

You will be joining as a Virtual Machine Monitor Engineer as part of the Monitor Group. The Monitor Group is a part of the VMWare Cloud Foundation (VCF) Division under Broadcom. This organization handles all aspects of virtual machine engineering and has deep roots in the history of the company. The Monitor Group is highly collaborative in nature, with a well-established culture of engineering discipline. Here you will have the opportunity not only to interact with other team members within the Group, but also other groups working on core aspects of vSphere. You will lead your part within the projects, as well as frequently be given the opportunity to present your work to others and learn about the novel work of other engineers.

Job Requirements

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or related field and 8+ years of related experience or Masters degree in Computer Science or related field and 6+ years of related experience or PhD plus 3+ years.
Experience in C, and assembly programming
Experience working on the kernel and /or virtualization space
Proficient in x86_64 CPU architecture

Must have legal authorization to work in the US.

jobs.description:

More recently, GPU deep learning ignited modern deep learning - the next era of computing - with the GPU acting as the brain of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can perceive and understand the world. Join us at the forefront of technological advancement.

What You’ll Be Doing

Own bring-up of new platforms in the factory across every level: board, tray, rack, and cluster. You will be the software owner from the first power-on, working alongside hardware, firmware, diagnostics, and test engineering.

Be the one who unblocks the line. When a station is down, trace the failure across hardware and software stacks to find and fix the root cause.

10+ years of experience in data center firmware, platform software or factory/manufacturing test software, with a BS, MS or PhD in EE, CS or a related field (or equivalent experience).
A proven track record building factory or data center automation (firmware flashing, diagnostics orchestration, provisioning, or log collection) and out-of-band management for large-scale server deployments.
Strong Python skills for building production tools and orchestration frameworks, plus working knowledge of C/C++, shell and Linux systems.
Solid knowledge of hardware interfaces (PCIe, USB, SMBus/I2C) and of debugging servers during early bringup.
Experience working directly with ODMs, CMs, or CSPs during NPI, bring-up, and volume production.
A strong communicator and collaborator who does well with ambiguity, owns problems end to end and works well across time zones.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Experience with rack-scale or multi-node GPU systems (NVLink switch trays, rack-level diagnostics, compute/switch tray bringup).
Familiarity with manufacturing diagnostic frameworks and factory test stations.
Experience designing resilient factory flows that improve first-pass yield and reduce line downtime.

jobs.description:
We are seeking a Linux Systems Engineer to join our Infrastructure Engineering team, dedicated to supporting high-performance EDA compute farms. You will be responsible for designing, deploying, and maintaining enterprise-grade Linux environments across RPM-based distributions, optimized for the high-throughput requirements of EDA workloads. You will drive automation initiatives, and build robust tooling to support a highly available and scalable infrastructure.

What You'll Be Doing

Linux Infrastructure Engineering: Maintain, tune, and secure mission-critical Linux operating systems across production and non-production environments.
End-to-End Automation: Lead infrastructure configuration management and continuous deployment workflows using Infrastructure as Code, e.g. Ansible and Terraform.
Tooling Development: Write high-quality, maintainable code in Python, Bash, or Go to automate repetitive operational tasks and integrate infrastructure telemetry.
Naming & Storage Services: Manage Linux Naming Services (LDAP/SSSD) and networked storage (NFS, Autofs) environments to support high-performance EDA workloads.

What We Need To See

Linux Internals: 8+ years of deep systems engineering experience working with RPM-based Linux distributions.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.
Infrastructure as Code: Strong track record of automating end-to-end multi-tier infrastructure configurations and managing centralized deployments. Experience with more than one configuration management system is a bonus.
Virtualization and Container Architecture: Deep understanding of virtualization and container internals (e.g., Docker, Podman, Kubernetes, MicroVMs), including trade-offs between technologies. Demonstrated ability to design and build scalable container infrastructure from scratch, including registry management, custom image development, and layer optimization.
Scripting & Tooling: Proficiency in at least one modern language (Python, Rust, or Go) for infrastructure automation, tooling development, and API integrations.
Networking Fundamentals: Deep operational understanding of OSI layers, TCP socket states, MTU optimization, packet captures (tcpdump, wireshark), and modern physical or software-defined networking (SDN).

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Experience with CI/CD integration pipelines (GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, or Jenkins) for infrastructure artifacts. Relevant industry certifications (e.g., RHCE, CKA).
Proven experience managing GCP and AWS compute services Experience with using LLMs to build and manage infrastructure
Prior experience supporting EDA toolchains (e.g., Synopsys, Cadence) and high-performance compute clusters (e.g. exposure to LSF and Slurm environments a bonus)

The Codex Core Agents team builds the agent harness that turns model capability into real-world action. This team sits close to research and works across the stack: harness, model interaction, inference, sandboxed execution, orchestration, evals, production reliability, and the performance envelope around tokens, latency, cost, capacity, and quality. The harness is open source and increasingly part of how models are trained and evaluated, making this one of the highest-leverage layers in Codex.

About The Role

We’re looking for engineers to build the AI systems that make Codex agents dependable in production. The ideal candidate is an agent-systems builder: hands-on across low-level systems and ML workflows, able to debug Codex behavior end to end across the harness, model behavior, inference/runtime stack, GPU fleet, and product surface.

You’ll work with research, infrastructure, and product to design agent harness capabilities, run experiments and ablations across the model + system prompt + harness stack, build frameworks for assessing production agent performance, and turn messy failures into durable improvements.

Build sandboxing, isolation, orchestration, state, and workflow infrastructure for agents operating in real development environments.
Develop evaluation, experimentation, and debugging systems that distinguish harness issues, model behavior, inference/runtime issues, and product failures.
Run ablations across prompts, model-facing interfaces, context construction, tool-use strategies, and harness behavior to improve solve rate, reliability, latency, and cost.
Improve observability, profiling, and diagnostics across the agent stack, from backend systems to inference, GPUs, and fleet capacity.
Work closely with research to make the harness trainable, measurable, and useful for improving frontier agentic models.
Build shared primitives that make Codex faster, safer, more reliable, and easier for other teams and open-source users to build on.

Have built or operated production systems in distributed systems, infrastructure, developer tooling, sandboxing, virtualization, cloud platforms, or ML systems.

jobs.title: Platform Engineer
jobs.description:
Why This Role

Concourse is building the operating system for State and Local governments. Our platform is a configurable approach to tackling fragmented government data and workflows and turning them into smooth operations for public servants and the constituents they serve. As a Concourse Platform Engineer, you're not building a marginal feature for one product. You're contributing to the infrastructure that scales to our hundreds of products serving millions of Americans.

You own the foundational layer: the data ingestion pipelines, AI workflow orchestration engine, and configurable primitives that support everything above them. Your role is to empower our Forward-Deployed PMs who sit alongside city and county teams, understand their specific workflows, and assemble each agency's solution. A bail management system for a county courthouse. IT Helpdesk for a school district. A water utility operations dashboard. An ERP for a mid-sized city. The FDPMs build those. Your job is to make sure they can.

You're working on the deep infrastructure questions that make every deployment possible: how to reliably ingest data from a 30-year-old mainframe, how to run multi-step AI workflows that government users can audit and trust, how to expose primitives flexible enough to model any government process but constrained enough that non-engineers can build on them.

These are hard, novel problems. The people solving them will define the next generation of government software serving us.

What You'll Do

Design and own the connectors, ingestion pipelines, and data modeling primitives that normalize government data from legacy systems (mainframes, Oracle, flat files, proprietary APIs) into a consistent, queryable foundation
Build the infrastructure for long-running, multi-step AI workflows: task queuing, state management, retries, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, and the audit trails government compliance requires
Build and maintain the core primitives FDPMs build on top of: the workflow engine, role-based access model, form and action framework, and event system that let a non-engineer assemble a bail system or permitting platform without writing the plumbing from scratch
Bake in data isolation, access controls, and auditability as core platform features from the start, with a path toward compliance certifications (FedRAMP, CJIS, HIPAA) as we grow
Work directly with the founder on architecture decisions that will compound across every deployment we ever ship

What We're Looking For

A portfolio: what have you built end-to-end, from scratch, under pressure?
Strong backend fluency in Python and/or Node, with solid instincts for data modeling, API design, and building systems that stay reliable and extensible over time
Enough frontend ability to build and reason about a UI, even if you won't own it
Hands-on experience using AI coding tools (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Factory, etc.) as a core part of your daily workflow
Good instincts for abstraction: knowing when to generalize something into a platform primitive vs. when to just ship it
US citizen (required for government work)
Willing to work in-person in Flatiron, NYC (5 days/week)

Nice to have:

Experience building developer platforms or internal tooling, devops/infrastructure, agentic AI orchestration, or work in regulated industries like healthcare, finance, or legal.

About Concourse

Concourse is the fastest-growing govtech, providing software to more than 100 state and local governments across the U.S.

Government calls what we do "IT modernization." We call it a trillion-dollar opportunity to overhaul how government works. Public services are broken not because of bureaucracy but instead because they run on antiquated, user-unfriendly software from legacy vendors.

Some examples: Concourse is powering the legislative management system for one of America's largest cities, a state's entire online bail payment system, and a case-management platform for mental-health response teams.

We are an AI-native company. Our org structure and staffing model are radically different from those of legacy tech companies: we have a flat team of superstar generalists who both own client relationships and manage fleets of long-horizon AI agents.

Our team works together in our Flatiron office five days a week.

Compensation Range: $160K - $200K

Position Summary

The Delivery Engineer is an early-career technical role for engineers and other builders who want to develop broad expertise across technology, customer delivery, and product.

Delivery Engineers are aligned to a state or customer rather than a single product. Working alongside experienced technical and delivery leaders, they develop an end-to-end understanding of how Pearson's platforms, integrations, data flows, and operational processes work together to meet customer requirements and contractual commitments.

This is a hands-on role. Delivery Engineers demonstrate solutions, investigate technical issues, validate integrations, support implementations and production events, and work across teams to drive problems toward resolution. The role provides broad exposure to customers, products, and technology organizations and is designed to develop future leaders across Technology Readiness, Technical Product Management, Product Management, Delivery, Implementation, Support, and Technology.

Key Responsibilities

Develop deep knowledge of assigned state or customer programs, including requirements, contractual commitments, technical solutions, integrations, configurations, and operational processes.

Build and maintain an end-to-end understanding of the customer solution across test administration, test delivery, scoring, reporting, data exchange, identity, infrastructure, and external integrations.

Translate customer, RFP, and contractual requirements into technical requirements, solution approaches, validation criteria, and delivery considerations.

Create and maintain system diagrams, integration flows, data flows, and other technical documentation that clearly explains how the customer solution works.

Develop the product and solution knowledge needed to confidently explain and demonstrate Pearson's technology capabilities to customers and internal stakeholders.

Participate in customer technical discussions, demonstrations, integration reviews, solution workshops, and RFP or proposal activities.

Provide hands-on technical support during implementation, integration testing, readiness activities, administration windows, production events, and customer escalations.

Investigate technical issues across systems by analyzing configurations, APIs, integrations, data flows, logs, and system behavior.

Partner across Engineering, Product, Quality Engineering, Implementation, Operations, Support, Security, and Infrastructure to resolve technical issues and delivery risks.

Support end-to-end validation to ensure systems, integrations, and operational processes collectively meet customer requirements and commitments.

Identify technical gaps, dependencies, risks, and product limitations, and help ensure they are understood and addressed by the appropriate teams.

Apply lessons from implementations, incidents, and customer feedback to improve products, documentation, processes, and future customer solutions.

Required Qualifications

1 to 3 years of experience in software engineering, systems engineering, technical support, quality engineering, or another hands-on technology discipline, or equivalent experience building, testing, integrating, or operating software systems.

Practical experience with software applications, APIs, integrations, data flows, cloud-based systems, or related enterprise technologies.

Experience troubleshooting technical issues using structured problem-solving and technical evidence.

Ability to read technical documentation and create or interpret system diagrams, integration flows, and data flows.

Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts to technical and nontechnical audiences.

Strong technical curiosity, problem-solving skills, and interest in understanding how complex systems work together.

Interest in working directly with customers and developing confidence in customer-facing technical discussions and demonstrations.

Experience with APIs, cloud platforms, identity and access management, logging and monitoring tools, or distributed applications.

Experience supporting customer implementations, integration testing, production systems, incident response, or technical escalations.

Experience in enterprise technology, education technology, government, or large-scale assessment.

Exposure to RFPs, proposals, product management, solution engineering, implementation, or delivery functions.

Successful Delivery Engineers are curious, hands-on problem solvers who want to understand both the customer and the technology. They communicate clearly, collaborate effectively across teams, ask thoughtful questions, surface risks, and stay engaged until problems are resolved.

**Who We Are**

SmartRent (NYSE: SMRT) is revolutionizing how people live and work with the industry's only end-to-end platform designed for the rental housing industry. By uniting purpose-built software, integrated hardware and full implementation and support in one ecosystem, we help owners and operators simplify operations, cut costs and deliver exceptional resident experiences. Recognized by Deloitte, HousingWire and the PropTech Breakthrough Awards, SmartRent is shaping the future of property technology and redefining what it means to make rental housing smarter.

**Job Description**

You own the mobile platform layer: the native module boundary, the build and release pipeline, and the performance and stability budgets. Feature engineers ship on top of what you build, and your work is measured by how fast they can do that without writing one-off bridge code.

This is a hands-on IC role. You will work in Swift and Kotlin for native code and in JavaScript most days. You decide when a device integration becomes a shared native module instead of a one-off, and you say no when it should stay in JS.

*Candidate based in Phoenix, AZ is preferred to come to our headquarters in North Phoenix on a hybrid schedule.*

  

**Responsibilities**

* Design and maintain the shared native modules that power device control and other hardware-specific features across our apps
* Plan, sequence, and schedule React Native and native platform upgrades, including related dependency work, without stalling feature delivery
* Own the iOS and Android build, signing, and store submission process, and keep it documented so any engineer on the squad can cut a release and new engineers can build on day one
* Define targets for crash-free session rate, cold start time, and binary size; instrument and alert on them; and advocate for them in planning when a feature puts one at risk
* Partner with backend teams early on payload shape, pagination, real-time device state, and error semantics before APIs are built
* Set code review standards, mentor other mobile engineers, and document technical decisions so they outlast the conversation
* Collaborate with other squads on shared mobile patterns, and with Product, QA, Customer Success, and Marketing on release scope and timing

  

**Required Qualifications**

* 8+ years of professional software engineering experience, including 5+ years shipping mobile apps on both the App Store and Google Play
* 3+ years of production React Native experience, including building and maintaining native modules

Heaviside Industries builds multi-domain autonomous precision munitions for U.S. and allied special operations and conventional forces. While modern warfare has rapidly evolved with the proliferation of unmanned systems, hyper-precise munitions in contested environments are the future of the battlefield. Economical precision strike capabilities are critical to U.S. and allied war efforts, enabling successful defeat of enemy military assets and infrastructure. We are seeking an expert Embedded Software / Firmware Contractor to design, implement, and optimize high-throughput multi-threaded software for embedded Linux on AMD Xilinx FPGA / MPSoC and RFSoc architectures (e.g., Zynq UltraScale+).
  
The contractor will be responsible for accelerating critical computational workloads (such as signal processing or array arithmetic) using ARM NEON SIMD instructions and interfacing custom C/C++ applications with hardware IP blocks in the FPGA logic. Scope of Work & Deliverables
  
High-Performance Multi-Threading: Architect and implement efficient C/C++ userspace applications utilizing POSIX threads (pthreads), thread isolation, CPU affinity, and lock-free synchronization routines to handle real-time streaming data on embedded Linux.
  
ARM NEON Optimization: Vectorize and optimize critical algorithmic loops using ARM NEON intrinsics and assembly to maximize SIMD throughput on ARM Cortex-A processor cores.
  
FPGA Hardware Integration: Develop robust software drivers/interfaces (e.g., Linux UIO, AXI DMA, memory-mapped registers) to exchange data between Linux software applications and custom IP blocks in the Xilinx Programmable Logic (PL).
  
Profiling & Performance Tuning: Utilize Linux profiling tools (perf, Valgrind, custom execution benchmarks) to diagnose bottlenecks, optimize cache usage, and ensure deterministic performance.
  
Technical Documentation & Code Hand-off: Deliver well-commented, productiongrade source code along with architectural notes, integration build scripts, and test procedures for internal engineering hand-off.

**Required Technical Expertise:**  
Core Programming: Expert-level C for embedded Linux environments.
  
Vector Acceleration: Hands-on proficiency with ARM NEON SIMD intrinsics and assembly-level optimization techniques.
  
Xilinx SoC Platform: Demonstrated experience with Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC/RFSoC platforms (PetaLinux).
  
Hardware Interfacing: Deep understanding of AXI4, PCIe, AXI DMA engines, and Linux memory management (DMA-BUF, /dev/mem, UIO).
  
Multi-Threaded Systems: Solid background in concurrent programming, memory synchronization, and real-time POSIX scheduling.
  
Tooling: Expertise with GCC/Clang cross-compilation toolchains, GDB, Vivado / Vitis, CMake, and Git.

#### **Who are we?**

Longshot Space Technologies is at the cutting edge of low-cost space access and hypersonics. We are developing a novel space launch system that accelerates mass over a long distance. Using our technology, we plan to provide affordable launch services for satellites, cargo, and future space infrastructure. Our mission is to enable a future where humans can reach for the stars.

#### **Position Overview**

We are hiring a Staff Electrical Engineer to own electrical engineering across Longshot, including the people, the architecture and the hardware. You will provide leadership and expertise in defining system architecture and electronics platforms for high-voltage pulsed ignition, firing and sequencing control, instrumentation and data acquisition, safety interlocks, vehicle avionics and power, and test site power. Deliverables include circuit card assemblies (CCAs), FPGA and microprocessor designs, harnesses, and the test procedures and scripts that verify them.

The electrical team is small and works across every program. You will set its technical direction, grow it, and be the accountable owner for electrical design at design reviews and test readiness. This is a hands-on lead role: you will design and review schematics, be in the bunker on test day, and sign your name to what goes on the launcher.

#### **Job Details**

* Role Type: Full-time
* Compensation: $180,000 to $220,000 per year
* Location: Alameda, CA Onsite with 25%-30% travel for campaigns

#### **Key Responsibilities** **Architecture and design**

* Derive and document engineering requirements, specifications and interface definition drawings for electrical assemblies.
* Define and control interfaces with mechanical, software, test and facilities teams.
* Define requirements for, and guide the design and implementation of, FPGAs, microcontrollers and embedded electronics for control and test systems.

**Test, verification and documentation**

**Safety and reviews**

* Drive design for safety in high-energy systems: energy storage, safe/arm, fault tolerance, isolation, discharge and lockout/tagout.
* Act as electrical authority on hazard analyses.

* Participate in development of contract technical documentation for government-funded programs.
Provide technical insight and oversight of subcontracts and key suppliers.

* BS in Electrical Engineering with 6+ years of related work experience, MS in a similar discipline with 4+ years, or PhD with 3+ years
* Strong background in design and/or analysis of analog, digital and power circuits, in one or more of pulsed power / high-voltage systems, ignition or initiation systems, test-stand control and instrumentation, or flight avionics and power
* Experience across the full design cycle from requirements through schematic, layout review, harness, build, test and field support
* Command of high-energy safety practice: energy storage hazards, interlocks, grounding and shielding, EMI in noisy high-current environments

* Flexible and accountable: meets commitments and produces quality products within budget through effective prioritization
* Experience with configuration management tools (e.g., Git, Jira)

* Exceptional interpersonal skills, working effectively with internal and external program leadership and with every level of the team, from technicians to customers

Desire to be hands-on, on-site and at the test stand  

#### **Preferred Qualifications**

**Electrical Engineer**

**Endiatx, Inc. · Hayward, California · Full-time**

**About Endiatx**

Endiatx is a medical device company developing medical robotic systems for diagnostic use inside the human body. Our flagship platforms include PillBot™, a propeller-driven endoscopic capsule designed to enable real-time visualization of the stomach, and PillVue™, a passive capsule endoscopy system designed to improve access to gastrointestinal diagnostics.  
We are a multidisciplinary team of engineers, clinicians, and operators building a new category of medical diagnostics at the intersection of robotics, imaging, and AI.

**Role Summary**

We are hiring an Electrical Engineer to design, prototype, and test compact, low-power electronic hardware for our medical device platforms. You will develop circuit boards and electrical subsystems with a focus on battery power management, motor drivers, and integration with imaging and communication interfaces.

This is a hands-on role spanning schematic design, PCB development, board bring-up, laboratory debugging, and system integration. You will work closely with Firmware, Software, Mechanical, Mechatronics, Manufacturing, and Quality teams to deliver reliable hardware and documented test results.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Translate system requirements into electrical specifications, circuit architectures, and component selections.

* Design analog, digital, and mixed-signal circuits, including power supplies, sensor interfaces, and motor-control circuitry as needed.

* Own schematic design and PCB development through release, including layout execution or direction and review of layout resources, grounding, signal integrity, thermal behavior, and test access.

* Perform board bring-up and debug circuits using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, multimeters, and laboratory power supplies.

When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

**About the Role:**

Crusoe Cloud runs AI infrastructure at a scale where a single firmware or software baseline can determine whether thousands of GPUs deliver for our customers. As a Staff Technical Program Manager, you will own the end-to-end release lifecycle for versioned firmware and software baselines across our GPU fleet. That covers everything from scoping and qualification through phased rollout and production deployment. This is a builder role: you will run complex releases across Compute, Networking, Storage, Orchestration, and Operations, and you will design the release calendars, validation frameworks, and metrics that let Crusoe scale them predictably.

We’re looking for an engineer-rooted TPM who is comfortable in the white space between teams and who earns trust with engineers and vendors through technical depth and execution rigor. You’ll identify risks before they surface, drive alignment across engineering leads without direct authority, and give leadership clear, data-driven decision points. This is a full-time position.

**What You'll Be Working On:**

* **Own the Release Lifecycle End to End:** Lead versioned firmware and software baselines from scoping and definition through qualification, validation, phased rollout, and production deployment across a large GPU fleet.
* **Orchestrate Cross-Functional Releases:** Drive release programs across Compute, Networking, Storage, Orchestration, and Operations. Set entry and exit criteria, layered validation, domain sign-offs, and go/no-go decisions.
* **Lead Fleet-Wide Upgrade Campaigns:** Coordinate upgrades on live production clusters with Operations and customer-facing teams, including maintenance planning, rollback strategies, and risk mitigation.
* **Drive Security and CVE Response:** Partner with engineering leads to make fast, well-reasoned decisions on security patches and CVEs, and fold them into the release train.
* **Govern Vendor Relationships:** Work with OEMs, ODMs, and component and silicon suppliers on firmware fixes, validation timelines, and roadmaps. Escalate and resolve issues that put Crusoe’s schedule at risk.
* **Build the Machine:** Design lightweight, scalable release calendars, validation frameworks, Jira workflows, and metrics that make Crusoe’s release process predictable as the fleet grows.
* **Surface Risk and Drive Decisions:** Maintain real-time visibility into release health, map cross-team dependencies, and deliver crisp executive updates that spotlight decisions and trade-offs.
* **Improve Continuously:** Lead retrospectives after major releases and feed the learnings back into the process. Apply AI tools to improve tracking, risk detection, and communication across your programs.

**What You'll Bring to the Team:**

* **Program Leadership at Scale:** 10+ years as a Technical Program Manager in infrastructure, hardware, or platform engineering, including release or change management at fleet scale.
* **Server Firmware Expertise:** Working knowledge of the server firmware stack, including BMC, BIOS, GPU firmware and drivers, and NIC and switch firmware.
* **Influence Without Authority:** Proven experience running validation or qualification programs across many engineering teams without direct authority.
* **Risk and Dependency Management:** Ability to anticipate what will break before it does, then drive mitigation plans and rollback strategies for live production environments.
* **Process Builder’s Mindset:** Track record of creating fit-for-purpose frameworks, such as release calendars, validation gates, and metrics, rather than forcing programs into rigid templates.
* **Executive Communication:** Ability to translate complex technical status into clear, data-driven updates and decision-ready recommendations.
* **Educational Foundation:** Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience.

**Bonus Points**

* Experience at a GPU cloud provider or hyperscaler managing large-scale fleets (thousands of nodes).
* A track record of driving firmware currency and compliance programs across a production fleet.
* Hands-on experience with vendor escalation management, including driving OEM/ODM and silicon partners to fix and validate firmware on tight timelines.
* Familiarity with AI accelerator platforms and the dependencies between firmware, drivers, and cluster networking.
* A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.

**Benefits:**

* Employer contributions to HSA account
* Paid parental leave

* Observability tooling (metrics/logs/traces), capacity/performance tuning, and cost/tiering practices for storage platforms.

Job Title: Systems Hardware Design Engineer

**Experience:** 3+ years  
**Department:** Hardware Engineering / R&D  
**Employment Type:** Full-Time  
**Location:** On-site in Irvine, California  
**Salary Range:** $100,000 – $150,000 per year, based on experience

**About Omnitron**

Omnitron Systems Technology designs and manufactures fiber media converters, PoE switches, single pair Ethernet products, and network demarcation devices that keep critical networks running. Headquartered in Irvine, California, we design and manufacture all of our products in the United States, and they are trusted and used by government agencies, utilities, data centers, process automation, security surveillance, and service providers. As a focused, engineering-driven company, our hardware engineers see their designs through from concept to production, working closely with the various cross functional teams.

**Job Summary**

We are seeking a motivated and technically skilled Systems Hardware Design Engineer to design, develop, test, and validate electronic hardware systems. The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience in digital and analog circuit design, schematic capture, and supervising PCB layout. The engineer will be responsible for the complete hardware development lifecycle, from system-level requirements and circuit design through PCB layout, prototype bring-up, debugging, verification, and product release.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Own hardware design from requirements to release. Define system architecture, design digital, analog, mixed-signal, and power supply circuits, and create schematics in industry-standard EDA tools.
* Select components such as microcontrollers, processors, interfaces, sensors, and power devices, using datasheet review and trade-off analysis.
* Supervise outsourced PCB layout. Set placement, stackup, routing, and impedance constraints; review layouts for grounding, power distribution, and signal integrity; and approve fabrication and assembly files.
* Lead board bring-up of prototype and production hardware using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and other lab equipment.
* Plan and run verification, validation, and qualification testing, including functional, electrical, and performance tests.
* Drive design-for-manufacturing and design-for-test (DFM/DFT), and support production through fabrication, assembly, troubleshooting, and continuous improvement.
* Produce and maintain design documentation: schematics, BOMs, test reports, engineering change records, and production transition documents (assembly, test, and programming instructions).
* Work closely with firmware, FPGA, mechanical, systems, manufacturing, and test teams, including leading design reviews.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field.
* Strong fundamentals in analog and digital electronics, including circuit analysis, component behavior, signal conditioning, and power management.
* Experience with microcontroller-based designs and common interfaces such as SPI, I²C, UART, USB, and Ethernet.
* Hands-on schematic capture and a command of PCB layout principles (grounding, decoupling, impedance control, routing, EMI/EMC), plus experience managing external layout, fabrication, and assembly vendors.
* Proven hardware debugging skills with standard lab instruments, and the ability to own designs independently while working closely with a multidisciplinary team.
* Experience with EMC compliance testing, ESD protection, and electrical safety.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* FPGA development in Verilog or VHDL, including simulation, synthesis, and timing analysis.
* High-speed digital and mixed-signal design, including signal integrity, power integrity, DC-DC converters, LDOs, and power sequencing.
* Networking or ruggedized hardware, such as Ethernet PHYs and switches, fiber optic transceivers (SFP), PoE, or industrial-temperature electronics.
* EDA tools such as Altium Designer, Cadence Allegro/OrCAD, Siemens Xpedition, or KiCad.

* Salary range of $100,000 – $150,000 per year, based on experience.
* 401(k) with profit sharing and health benefits.
* Opportunities to work across the complete hardware product development lifecycle.
* Hands-on exposure to challenging electronic design and system integration projects.
* Collaboration with experienced engineers across hardware, firmware, FPGA, and systems disciplines.
* Opportunities for technical growth and increasing design ownership based on experience.

jobs.title: Senior/Staff Hardware Design Engineer
jobs.description:
**What to Expect**
==================

Heron Power is a startup company building cutting-edge power electronics for the 21st-century grid. We aim to debottleneck the growth of electricity generation and consumption with scalable, innovative, and less costly hardware solutions, accelerating the electrification of everything.

Our first goal is to build better converters (inverters & rectifiers) to connect large-scale renewables, storage, and loads like datacenters to the grid. Heron Power’s leadership team is made up of seasoned veterans who have designed and shipped gigawatts of power conversion products over the past decade.

We understand that no one individual knows everything. We will all learn *a lot* together and from each other. We strive to build a collaborative, enriching environment conducive to personal, technical, and career growth. You can expect to work in a dynamic and collaborative environment, driven by first principles engineering, solving difficult problems.

**Job Overview**
================

As an Senior/Staff Hardware Design Engineer, you will be responsible for architecting, designing, and integrating the low voltage electrical system within high-performance power converters to meet reliability, EMC, and safety requirements. You will define cabinet-level electrical architecture, manage harnessing and interconnects, and ensure proper distribution of power, signals, and control across subsystems. Your work will span the full product lifecycle—from concept development and component selection to schematic capture, validation, and support through production.

**How You Will Contribute**
===========================

* *Own the full hardware development lifecycle—from requirements definition and modeling through schematic capture, PCB layout, prototyping, testing, validation, and manufacturing support.*
* *Define and implement the low voltage electrical architecture for cabinet-based systems, including cabinet microprocessors, power supplies, power distribution, interconnects, and signal processing and routing.*
* *Select appropriate LV components such as microcontrollers, interface circuits, fuses, relays, contactors, terminal blocks, and power supplies based on system requirements and reliability targets.*
* *Create system block diagrams, schematics, and harness documentation to support cross-functional development and manufacturing.*
* *Ensure electrical interface integrity across PCBs, sensors, actuators, and communication buses (e.g., CAN, RS-485, Ethernet, LV analog/digital I/O).*
* *Collaborate with mechanical teams on enclosure layout, cable routing, shielding, and grounding strategies for EMI/EMC performance.*
* *Support validation and bring-up of LV systems during prototype and production builds, including DVT and integration testing.*
* *Ensure compliance with safety and regulatory standards such as UL, CE, and IEC for low voltage systems.*
* *Coordinate with firmware, test, and manufacturing teams to ensure proper system behavior, integration, and serviceability.*

**What You Will Bring**
=======================

We’re open to candidates with both mid and senior-career experience. Scope and responsibilities will scale with the right candidate.

**Must-Have Requirements**
--------------------------

* *Degree in Electrical Engineering or related field.*
* *5+ years of experience in low voltage electrical system design, including cabinet-level LV system architecture and component designs, ideally in energy, automotive, or industrial control applications.*
* *Strong knowledge of cabinet-level LV power distribution and signal architecture.*
* *Experience selecting and integrating LV components (relays, fuses, terminal blocks, etc.) for multi-voltage systems (e.g., 12V, 24V, 48V).*
* *Familiarity with harness design, connector systems, and creating electrical schematics and wiring diagrams.*
* *Understanding of EMC best practices and grounding/shielding techniques.*
* *Proficiency with electrical CAD tools (e.g., Altium).*
* *Hands-on experience with debugging, testing, and validating electrical systems using oscilloscopes, multimeters, and similar tools.*
* *Experience with manufacturing processes, including design for manufacturability (DFM), volume production, and development of manufacturing test procedures and test equipment.*

**Nice-to-Haves**
-----------------

* *Experience with LV systems in high-voltage environments*
* *Familiarity with fieldbus communication protocols like CAN or industrial ethernet.*
* *Knowledge of control cabinet UL/IEC compliance and wire derating, spacing, and thermal considerations.*
* *Experience in creating wiring harnesses and managing cable assemblies with third-party suppliers.*
* *Exposure to cross-functional design with firmware and mechanical engineering teams.*
* *Experience with failure mode analysis and root cause investigations of LV electrical systems.*
* *Knowledge of safety-critical system design, including interlocks and redundant controls.*

If you are passionate about technology and enjoy working in a fast-paced environment, we would love to hear from you. Join us in accelerating the electrification of everything at Heron Power.

Heron Power provides competitive compensation (salary and equity) and benefits. The base salary for this role ranges from $140,000 to $200,000 per year.

jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century's most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril's family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

### **ABOUT THE TEAM**

Maritime Digital Production (MDP) is the software and digital systems function within Anduril's Heavy Metal division. We build and deploy the full technology stack that powers Anduril's shipbuilding factories: the data infrastructure that makes every machine and sensor visible in real time, the manufacturing execution system (ArsenalOS) that workers and planners use every shift, the scheduling engine that replans production in minutes instead of days, and the AI systems that eliminate manual toil from both the shop floor and business operations.  
  
MDP operates at the boundary between Operational Technology and Information Technology. Our systems live where factory-floor machines, edge compute, and OT networks meet enterprise platforms and cloud infrastructure. We incubate solutions close to the production line, validate them with real operators building real hardware, harden them for reliability and security, and then scale them across multiple sites. The environment is fast, physical, and consequential. When our systems go down, production stops. The output of our work is not a dashboard: it is a ship.  
  
This is not a support function. It is a strategic investment by Anduril in the premise that digitizing the manufacturing lifecycle end-to-end, from engineering definition through scheduling through execution through field feedback, is how Heavy Metal will out-build, out-adapt, and out-scale the traditional defense industrial base. MDP is scaling from a founding team to 70+ engineers across multiple U.S. sites. You will be joining early, working on hard problems with real operational stakes, and shaping how manufacturing software is built at Anduril from the ground up.

As a Senior Backend Software Engineer on the Systems Integrity Group (SIG) initiative, you will build simulation and digital twin validation frameworks that verify manufactured output matches engineering intent. You will develop applications powered by Unreal Engine 5 for 3D visualization, create V&V automation tooling, and build interfaces that give engineering and operations teams data-rich, walkable views of the factory and production systems.

* Build web applications that orchestrate simulation frameworks, digital twin validation, and V&V automation workflows for manufacturing verification.
* Develop UE5-based 3D visualization interfaces that ingest real-time data from the Unified Namespace and render data-rich, interactive views of factory operations, manufacturing processes, and production systems.
* Partner with manufacturing engineers and factory operators to understand production workflows and translate them into software requirements.
* Write production-quality code with comprehensive tests, participating in code review and architectural discussions.

* Develop automated V&V pipelines that run integration tests, validation checks, and compliance verification across design, manufacturing, and operations domains.
* Deploy and operate your systems in factory environments, including edge compute clusters and OT networks.

* Build responsive web interfaces for V&V dashboards, test management, requirements traceability, and system-level validation reporting.
* Leverage AI tooling (coding assistants, automation) in your development workflow and contribute to team engineering practices.
* Join an on-call rotation supporting production factory systems.
* Collaborate cross-functionally with simulation engineers, systems architects, backend engineers, and manufacturing teams to ensure seamless integration with MES, PLM, ERP, and enterprise systems.

### **REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* 6+ years of experience in a software engineering role building production systems, ideally in a fast-paced environment.
* Deep expertise in web development, with demonstrated mastery of backend systems.
* Strong technical fluency in modern software architectures, APIs, distributed systems, CI/CD, and cloud or edge infrastructure.

jobs.title: Director, Electrical Engineering
jobs.description:
Atomic Machines is building the Matter Compiler™, the first in a new class of AI-native, all-digital manufacturing systems that build working machines directly from code. The Matter Compiler (MC) is aimed at micro-machines: motors and gears the size of a grain of sand, robots small enough to work inside the body, cooling built directly into the chips that run AI, and the many devices like them that have been waiting on a way to build them. Its first product is PrimeSwitch™, an electromechanical power relay the size of a button battery that carries 150 amps continuous current and opens in 50 microseconds, about a thousand times faster than a conventional contactor. Founded by Jeff Holden — serial entrepreneur, ex-Amazon SVP and Uber's first Chief Product Officer — the company has raised $250 million to date.

Atomic Machines is based in the San Francisco Bay Area, with offices in Emeryville and Santa Clara.

### **About The Role:**

Atomic Machines is building autonomous manufacturing systems that combine a core robotics platform with a diverse set of manufacturing processes. As Director of Electrical Engineering, you'll lead Electrical Engineering in developing electronics and electrical architectures spanning core motion control hardware, sensor/actuator interfaces, and specialized manufacturing systems. You will also lead an Electrical Integration team in defining interconnect strategy and driving interconnect diagrams (ICDs), harness design and procurement, system bring-up, and integration.

You'll organize development across the core robotics platform and manufacturing process portfolio while building a cohesive, scalable electrical architecture. Working proactively with cross-functional partners, the CTO, and EE technical leaders, you'll uncover needs, align priorities, and balance shared platforms with process-specific designs.

### **What You'll Do:**

* Shape electrical engineering strategy across the core robotics platform and manufacturing process portfolio. Proactively uncover cross-functional needs and translate them into a roadmap, priorities, resource plans, and clear commitments.

* Provide deep technical leadership. Lead rigorous design reviews, challenge assumptions, and guide engineers through consequential tradeoffs and difficult technical problems.

* Take projects from problem identification through prototyping, implementation, and iteration.
* Build lightweight, maintainable tools that can be deployed quickly and improved based on real-world feedback.
* Proactively identify opportunities where software, data, or AI can improve the company's efficiency and capabilities.
